Snapped Labels

Published surface labels of four Herculaneum scrolls, moved along their normals onto the papyrus surface in the CT. Orange is the published label, blue is where it lands.

91%of vertices within 1 voxel of the recto face in a 1.129 µm scan, on 60 fresh PHerc0139 test sites. Published labels: 24%.
71%within 1 voxel on 60 fresh PHerc0814 test sites with the single-scan snap. Published labels: 24%.
+0.61 voxelscloser to the surface: a 3D surface model trained on snapped labels against the same model trained on published ones, scored on a scroll neither saw.
108segments on PHerc0139, PHerc0814, PHerc0841 and PHerc0172, as tifxyz meshes you can drop into VC3D or villa.

    What a snap does

    A surface label is a mesh (tifxyz: three float grids, x, y and z in scan voxels) that follows one wrap of papyrus. Traced labels sit near the sheet but rarely on it: on fresh test sites only about a quarter of published label vertices were within one voxel of the sheet's recto face. A snap moves each vertex along its mesh normal onto the face of the bright band nearest it, on the side toward the scroll's center line.

    Two methods

    • finesnap (PHerc0139, PHerc0814, PHerc0841): the label's own 9.4 µm scan is registered, vertex by vertex, to a 2.4 µm scan of the same scroll, and the face is found there. Where that fails, the label scan's own face is used (source.tif says which).
    • labelsnap (PHerc0172): the face is found in the label's own 7.9 µm scan.

    How it was measured

    Truth is the recto face seen in an independent 1.129 µm scan, at test sites drawn after the method was fixed and never used before. PHerc0139, 60 sites: within 1 voxel 23.7% for the published labels, 79.4% for labelsnap, 91.2% for finesnap. PHerc0814, 60 sites: 24.2% for published labels, 71.0% for labelsnap. A 3D surface model trained on snapped PHerc0139 labels placed the surface 0.61 voxels closer on PHerc0814 than the same model trained on published labels (95% interval 0.39 to 0.84; all 9 seed pairings).

    What is in each segment folder

    • snapped.tifxyz/: the moved mesh, same grid as the source; -1 where there is no vertex or it was held back.
    • abstain.tif: 0 snapped (face measured at the vertex), 1 not measured and left at its published position, 2 not measured and moved by the offset filled in from measured neighbors (filled), 255 no vertex or held back. Version 1.0.1 added code 2; in 1.0.0 filled vertices were 1.
    • confidence.tif (0 to 1), reason.tif (why no face was measured), source.tif (finesnap: 1 fine scan, 2 label scan).
    • release_mask.tif: 0 released, 1 held back for evaluation, 255 not in the source mesh. release.json: source URLs, checksums and the summary.

    Limits

    A snap moves along the normal only; it does not fix a label that follows the wrong wrap. Where two sheets touch, the face it finds can belong to the neighbor. Small regions are held back for evaluation and five segments of PHerc0139 and one of PHerc0841 are not included. The meshes are geometry: they say nothing about ink or text.

    Scans and source meshes: Vesuvius Challenge open data, CC BY-NC 4.0; the snapped meshes are shared under the same terms. Page code Apache 2.0. Made by Chase Hendrick.

    Connect your tool

    The snapped meshes, their records and the CT they sit on read straight from these URLs, logged out. Every segment is a tifxyz folder, so VC3D, villa and anything that reads tifxyz opens it as it is.

    Snapped labels: every segment, with index.json and checksums

    Python (numpy, tifffile)tested 2026-10-24 
    # pip install numpy tifffile
import io, json, urllib.request
import numpy as np, tifffile

T = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/vesuvius-snapped-labels/resolve/main/PHerc0841/20260220213127-w00/snapped.tifxyz"
meta = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(T + "/meta.json"))  # scale, bbox, format
get = lambda c: tifffile.imread(io.BytesIO(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{T}/{c}.tif").read()))
xyz = np.stack([get(c) for c in "xyz"], -1)  # xyz[i, j] = (x, y, z) in scan voxels; -1 = no surface

import zarr

root = zarr.open_group("https://vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/PHerc0841/volumes/20250821151531-9.366um-1.2m-113keV-masked.zarr", mode="r")  # OME-Zarr, zarr v2
